thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PROD alert: elevated 5xx + streaming timeouts on streaming-api (region: us-west). p95 latency doubled, p99 spiking. Investigate.

deploy-bot: Deployed release r2026.03.15-67 at 2024-11-07T17:10:12Z to streaming-api-canary -> streaming-api-stable.
javier: saw the alert, joining. What’s the error pattern? 5xx or client disconnects?
mia: logs show `upstream_connect_timeout` and `504` at the gateway, also many `kvcache miss` logs during large concurrency bursts.
katy: checking traces -> tail requests show large wait on `send_request_to_runtime` (1000-2500ms). Runtime instances report high `accept_queue` latency.
anna: rollout window had batching/continuous-batch flag enabled in config v2.1.1 -> might be causing head-of-line inferences. Rolling back that flag in canary earlier today showed no issues.
ops-lead: @javier @mia if this is a regression from the deploy, we should halt traffic and rollback. Customers are seeing elevated errors (support pinging).
javier: Agreed. Quick check: `kubectl get pods -l app=streaming-api -n prod -o wide` -> many pods in Running but CPU usage normal; GPU queues high (nvml shows long device queue time).
mia: Temp mitigation: shift traffic to regional fallback in eu-central and apply rate limit on streaming endpoints. I can update route table to force-routing: `redwoodctl route shift streaming-api --to eu-central --pct 0`.
katy: Can we disable continuous batching feature toggle without full rollback? Toggle name `enable_continuous_batching`. A/B toggle is in deployments config service.
anna: I can toggle it but prefer rollback of release to be faster (we saw immediate p99 improvement after previous rollback in staging). Command: `redwoodctl releases rollback streaming-api --to r2026.03.14-58`.
ops-lead: Start rollback. @deploy-bot kick it off and notify customers.
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by anna -> `redwoodctl releases rollback streaming-api --to r2026.03.14-58`. Rolling pods with rollout strategy Canary=0. ETA ~2min.
mia: Applying routing shift to reduce new sessions to affected instances and rate-limit streaming sessions to 10r/s per-user. Doing now.
katy: Observability: dashboards show p99 dropping within 90s on the first rolled-back pod. Link: <https://console.redwood/obs/dashboards/streaming-api?range=5m>
javier: Confirming reduction in 5xx from 8.2% -> 0.6% since rollback started. Still monitoring for residual kv cache warmups.
anna: Noted support escalations from 3 customers (enterprise). Ops notified them with ETA.
ops-lead: Good. Prepare handoff: next oncall (katy) will monitor for 30m, then escalate to eng-sre for postmortem. Capture canary logs and flamegraphs.
mia: Captured a few runtime flamegraphs (s3://redwood-logs/incident-1738902468/flamegraphs/). Also saved kvcache stats: `kvcache_hit_rate=0.32` at peak.
katy: Adding runbook notes: suspected regression from continuous batching + KV miss amplification -> causes runtime accept queue backlog -> gateway timeouts. Will add to postmortem checklist.
javier: Any customer data loss or corrupt outputs? Support: no corrupted outputs, only timeouts/504s.
ops-lead: Marking incident as mitigated after rollback. Next steps: postmortem with RCA, timeline, and action items: revert batching default, improve canary thresholds for streaming, and add automatic rollback on accelerated p99.
anna: Filing postmortem ticket and assigning to eng-ml + eng-runtime. Ticket: https://jira.redwood/browse/RW-INC-1738902468
katy: I'll take 1st watch, will post status in 30m. :thumbsup:
anna: Thanks all. Closing on-call bridge unless new alerts spike.
oncall-bot: Incident transitioned to monitoring state. No active page.
